name: D'Arcy McGee's Irish Pub website
status: The restaurant is now closed. The portfolio demo preserves the work as an interactive case study with fictional data.
summary: A practical website and content-management experience for an Irish pub, focused on helping customers find the menu and discover Saturday-night live shows.
hugoRole: Worked at D'Arcy McGee's for three years, first as a waiter and then as a barman.
Designed, developed, deployed, and maintained the website.
Managed the business Google Workspace account.
Maintained menu content through a monthly arrangement, updating weekly specials sent by the chef.
background: The owner asked Hugo to build the business's first official website. Hugo's firsthand experience of the venue shaped its visual identity, priorities, and day-to-day content workflow.
businessProblem: Customers needed an easy way to view the menu online.
The pub needed a clearer way to promote Saturday-night live shows.
Menu updates should not depend on hardcoded content or replacing PDF files.
audiences: Local customers looking for the menu or upcoming live shows.
The pub team sending weekly specials and managing content.
Portfolio visitors exploring the preserved project.
goals: Make the menu easy to discover and read online.
Help customers discover Saturday-night live shows.
Make frequent menu updates practical for the business.
Create a warm, useful digital presence based on the real venue experience.
publicExperience: Customers can browse the menu and pub information online.
Customers can discover Saturday-night live shows.
The experience presents the pub in a welcoming, business-focused way.
adminWorkflow: The admin area was created so menu content would not be hardcoded or limited to PDF-only updates.
The chef sent weekly specials and Hugo updated them as part of the monthly maintenance arrangement.
This made recurring content management easier and more consistent.

aiAssistedMenuImport.description: A real usability experiment let a user upload a menu image, extract individual items, review them, and then add them to the system.
aiAssistedMenuImport.result: It reduced a menu-update task from about 30 minutes manually to under five minutes.

reservations.policy: Reservations were intentionally handled by phone.
reservations.reason: The venue did not have staff capacity to manage online booking requests.
reservations.future: A booking feature could be considered if the business's operations and staffing changed.

impact: Local online visibility grew from a few hundred monthly visits initially to over 2,000 monthly visits over time.
The website made the menu and live-show information easier for customers to discover.
The website should not be described as directly generating revenue, bookings, or profit.
technologyOverview: A responsive public website paired with an admin area for menu and event content.
A content workflow designed around recurring menu updates and review before publishing.
The portfolio presentation is an interactive preservation of the project rather than a connection to the original system.

portfolioDemo.description: The demo is an interactive preservation of the project for portfolio visitors.
portfolioDemo.safety: Visitor changes stay local and never affect any real system.
portfolioDemo.disclosure: It is not the live restaurant system.

faq.question: What problem did this project solve?
faq.answer: It gave the pub its first official website so customers could view the menu online and discover Saturday-night live shows.

faq.question: Why did Hugo build the admin dashboard?
faq.answer: The dashboard avoided hardcoded menu content and PDF-only updates, making weekly specials easier to review and publish.

faq.question: How did the AI menu import help?
faq.answer: It let someone upload a menu image, extract and review individual items, and add them to the system. The experiment reduced the task from about 30 minutes to under five minutes.

faq.question: Was online reservation available?
faq.answer: No. Reservations were intentionally handled by phone because the venue did not have staff capacity for online booking requests.

faq.question: Are the demo data real?
faq.answer: No. The portfolio demo uses fictional data, and visitor changes stay local without affecting any real system.

faq.question: Why is the restaurant not operating now?
faq.answer: D'Arcy McGee's later closed after years of operation. The portfolio demo preserves the work as an interactive case study.

faq.question: What did Hugo do on this project?
faq.answer: He designed, developed, deployed, and maintained the website, managed the business Google Workspace account, and maintained menu content.

faq.question: What was the impact of the website?
faq.answer: Local online visibility grew from a few hundred monthly visits initially to over 2,000 monthly visits over time. The website should not be credited with directly generating revenue or bookings.
